scope.description: An open-subject linear direction that models form with precise contour and directional parallel or crossing strokes. Line density carries value, volume, and material on a light paper ground rather than acting as uniform surface noise.
limitations: Follow the requested subject, object count, and materials; do not add religious scenes, armor, animals, tools, or symbolic objects by default.
Vary line direction and density with the form; avoid filling every region with cross-hatching.

rules.instruction: Establish each requested subject with a readable, carefully varied contour; place interior lines only where they clarify construction, overlap, or a meaningful surface change.
rules.observable: The subject remains recognizable when reduced in size, and important edges are clearer than secondary texture.
rules.reject_when: Dense interior detail breaks the silhouette or every edge receives the same mechanical outline.
rules.avoid: uniform outlines, detail-first rendering, and lost silhouettes

rules.applies_when: The subject has a rounded, folded, recessed, or otherwise directional surface.
rules.instruction: Use spaced parallel strokes for light and middle values, then add a limited crossing layer for the deepest shadows; curve or turn the strokes with the form and leave paper breaks for highlights.
rules.observable: Value shifts are readable from changes in spacing and crossing density, while lit areas retain visible paper.
rules.reject_when: Cross-hatching covers the whole image uniformly, light areas turn gray, or hatch direction contradicts the form.
rules.avoid: uniform hatch carpets, gray-filled highlights, and form-blind line direction

rules.applies_when: The requested scene contains more than one visible material.
rules.instruction: Separate materials through stroke behavior: use longer directional marks for broad fabric or wood planes, shorter broken marks for rough surfaces, and controlled clean lines for hard edges; omit cues for materials absent from the prompt.
rules.observable: At least two requested materials can be distinguished by line grouping without adding photographic microtexture.
rules.reject_when: Every surface uses identical hatch marks or local marks become decorative noise.
rules.avoid: identical texture on all materials and scattered micro-detail

joint_checks.instruction: Keep contour, hatch direction, and material marks consistent with the same form and light; let clean paper remain visible wherever the subject is lit.
joint_checks.observable: The subject reads through contour first, line density then explains volume, and distinct materials use distinct but restrained mark groups.
